recipes.name: Harbour Dusk
recipes.description: The harbour an hour after the light goes: the blue end holds, the warm end is pulled back to a single ember, and the whole frame sits a little under. Both tones tightened over DR400 at 5000 K with red +1, clarity -3 and halation 30, on a film that drifts its reds one degree.
recipes.guidance: Water, wet streets and window light after sunset. It has nothing to give a bright noon.

recipes.name: Ember Curfew
recipes.description: Late neon on a warm negative, pushed. Saturation +3 at 6200 K with red +4, both tones lifted over DR100, halation 60 and a strong large grain that the recipe owns rather than borrowing from the camera.
recipes.guidance: Signs, tail lights and anything bright against a dark street.

recipes.name: Frost Mono
recipes.description: A cool monochrome for flat light: highlights pulled down, shadows opened, almost no halation and almost no vignette, so a grey day reads as tone rather than as murk. DR400 at 5200 K with blue +2.
recipes.guidance: Overcast, snow, and any day with no sun in it at all.
